why: A free function with a declared `this` parameter writes its receiver as it writes a parameter it changes: the write rebuilds the receiver record, the function returns it beside its result, and a caller passing a name through call or apply takes the new value back. mark returns the same value on both sides but stores the new count instead of the step: a changed receiver write, witnessed and not proved, and markTwice, which calls it twice and reads the count, changes with it. hit writes the same two fields in the same order through compound updates, and hitTwice passes the receiver through apply instead of call: proved. reset and resetAll are untouched: proved.
